summary: A fun, weekend-buildable concept, but there is no evidence anyone wants a watch-only AI date for their OC or would pay for it, and moderation plus companion-chatbot and contest-law exposure is heavy for a near-zero-overhead owner. The only reachable audience (pro-AI OC roleplayers) is narrow and may skew young or NSFW.

demand.evidence: No user has asked for this. RESEARCH.md cites Character.AI scale (~20M MAU, affiliate blogs) and Love Island's 25%+ prediction-game participation, which are adjacent behaviors, not demand for this product. No count of 'ship my OC' communities was found. Interest is not demand; the research rates confidence Low.

statusQuo.evidence: OC shippers already do this by hand in Discord/Reddit roleplay or Character.AI group chats, free and steerable. The habit is real, but 'creators can't steer' removes what many enjoy, and the workaround costs an evening of typing, not a painful loss.

specificity.evidence: Target is 'adults who make OCs and follow fictional relationship drama' plus friends: a category, no named person, community or size. Art-first OC communities reject AI (r/OriginalCharacter, itch.io thread), so the reachable segment is a pro-AI roleplay crowd of unknown size that RESEARCH.md says may skew young or NSFW.

wedge.evidence: M1 (one character, one house date, one prediction) is a real weekend build and free. But the value needs spectators and a second creator, so the smallest slice cannot show the core loop; a hand-run season is the only honest test.

futureFit.evidence: AI characters and fiction are commoditising; Character.AI could add an episode mode. Regulation (SB 243, FTC 6(b), age gating) is tightening around exactly this space. A shareable prediction habit is the only durable piece and it is unproven.

premises: OC creators want to watch their character in a story they cannot steer. Unsupported: no evidence; many enjoy steering.
A free prediction game drives spectator return. Partly supported by Love Island's participation, but that is a real cast with a TV audience.
Users will pay $3-$10 for premium characters, episode packs or cosmetics. Unsupported: all price evidence is chat subscriptions.
A watch-only show avoids companion-chatbot law and gambling rules. Unsettled; needs counsel.
Free models can write episodes funny and varied enough to hold a weekly audience. Untested.
alternatives: Minimal viable: single-player 'date my OC with a house character' page with a shareable episode card, no accounts, predictions or payments. A weekend, but tests novelty only.
Ideal architecture: the full creator + spectator + seasons platform in the PRD. Right long-term shape but needs a community, moderation and legal work first.
Lateral: run a hand-made season in an existing pro-AI roleplay Discord (20-50 OCs, episodes posted by David, predictions by emoji reaction) before writing any app.
Extend an existing repo: pettycourt (AI-judged story, friend voting, shareable card) already has the generate-then-vote mechanic; a dating-episode mode would reuse it.
wedge: One hand-run season in an existing pro-AI roleplay community: 20 OCs paired by David, episodes from a single prompt, followers predict via reactions. No app until requests for more episodes show up unprompted.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel Hobby + Neon/Turso free + free model via LiteLLM + Zod. The test that proves M1: POST /episodes with two valid characters returns a schema-valid episode (setting, two goals, twist, ending in the enum, at most 450 words) and returns 502 with nothing stored after two invalid model outputs. M3 payments need a commercial-use host, and the moderation filter is the real work, not the weekend.

risks: Moderation load (minors, NSFW, real people in character sheets) is incompatible with near-zero owner time.
California SB 243 and similar laws: private right of action of $1,000 per violation, scope for a watch-only show unsettled.
Contest and gambling rules: free points with paid cosmetics need a gaming lawyer.
Cold start: predictions are only fun with many spectators per episode.
Hostility from OC artists toward AI use of characters; the reachable audience is narrow.
Free-model episodes may turn repetitive so the weekly habit never forms.
No payment evidence for the game half of the product.
killCriteria: Drop it if a hand-run season gets fewer than 20 OC submissions, fewer than 25% of spectators predict a second episode, nobody asks for a next episode unprompted, counsel says SB 243 applies with obligations that cost money, or moderation needs more than an hour a week.

landing.headline: Send your original character on a blind date. Don't steer.
landing.subhead: Make an adult OC, let an AI showrunner write their blind date, and let friends predict how it ends. Free to play; points are just for bragging.
bullets: Your character, one blind date, written in minutes
You can't steer it, so the ending really surprises you
Friends guess: second date, friends or disaster
Free points with no value, never real-money betting
